title: Top K Frequent Elements
statement:
Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the `k` most frequent elements. You may return the answer in **any order**.

It is guaranteed that the answer is unique. Try to solve it in a time complexity better than O(n log n), where n is the array's size — a frequency count paired with bucket sort can get you to O(n).
constraints: k is in the range [1, the number of distinct elements in nums]
It is guaranteed that the answer is unique

examples.explanation: 1 appears 3 times, 2 appears 2 times, 3 appears once. The 2 most frequent are 1 and 2.

editorial.approach: First, build a frequency map of each number in `nums` using a hash map. Then use bucket sort: create an array of buckets indexed by frequency (from 0 to n), where bucket[f] holds every number that appears exactly f times. Walk the buckets from the highest frequency down to the lowest, collecting numbers until you have k of them. This avoids sorting the frequency map directly and runs in O(n) time. A heap-based approach (maintaining a min-heap of size k) also works in O(n log k) time.
editorial.complexity: O(n) time / O(n) space (bucket sort approach)
